question: An ancient oak has rotted hollow, leaving sound wood 30% of its radius thick. Treated as a tube, what percentage of its bending strength remains?
move: Material near the edge carries the load; the core mostly comes along.
trap: Assuming strength falls with the wood lost, to about half.
hint: The wood near the bark does most of the work when a trunk bends.
steps: The hollow's radius is 0.7 of the trunk's, so it removes 0.7² = 49% of the wood.
A tube's bending strength scales with R⁴ − r⁴ (outer and inner radius), not with its area of wood.
0.7⁴ = 0.24, so the hollow costs only 24% of the strength.
source: Mattheck & Breloer, Body Language of Trees
reference: Mattheck & Breloer, The Body Language of Trees: A Handbook for Failure Analysis, HMSO, 1994
